skill.name: sort-me-out
skill.description: Load when the user says "sort me out", "what am I missing", "what did I forget", "what's pending", "I'm all over the place", "ordéname", "qué me falta", "qué se me pasó", or asks for a full picture of everything open across projects, chats, clients and notes. The agent studies every source it can reach (notes, logs, task lists, memory, recent conversations, project files, live systems), then gives ONE ordered list: what is pending, what was promised and never done, what fell through the cracks, what is blocked and on whom, ranked by urgency and money at stake. For people who juggle many things and lose track.
skill.summary: Consolidate open work, forgotten commitments, and blockers into one prioritized list with owners and next actions.
skill.author: rabbitdesigns22

security_audit.summary: All three reconnaissance flags are false positives: they describe user-requested work review, service status verification, and invoice follow-up. A separate authorization risk exists because the skill directs execution of discovered tasks without requiring confirmation for every consequential action. No evidence found of credential theft, external exfiltration, or audit-manipulating prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Discovered tasks can be executed without explicit authorization beyond the initial review request.
remediation.suggestion: Default to a read-only review. Require explicit approval before changing files, contacting people, or modifying external systems, even for reversible or free actions.

content.user_title: Organize Open Work and Forgotten Commitments
content.value_statement: Tasks and promises become scattered across conversations, notes, and project records. This skill consolidates accessible context into a prioritized list with owners, blockers, and next actions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews accessible notes, conversations, task lists, and project records for unfinished work.
Checks current task status through available files, status pages, or APIs when access permits.
Merges duplicate tasks and distinguishes verified status from information found only in notes.
Identifies forgotten promises, overdue follow-ups, recurring duties, and financial priorities.
Organizes work into urgent, weekly, waiting, forgotten, and recently completed sections with owners and next actions.
Instructs the agent to save a timestamped review in project notes without storing secrets.
limitations: Provides instructions, not bundled integrations; access depends on the host agent, connected tools, and permissions.
Cannot guarantee complete coverage or verify records that are unavailable, outdated, or inaccessible.
Directs immediate execution of actionable tasks; users should explicitly require approval before changes or communications.
Saving review history requires a writable project notes location and can retain sensitive work context.

use_cases.title: Review Client Commitments
use_cases.description: Collect client promises, unpaid invoices, and neglected quotes into a prioritized follow-up list.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Team Work Review
use_cases.description: Consolidate issue trackers and project notes to identify blockers, responsible people, and the next required actions.

use_cases.title: Recover Unfinished Technical Work
use_cases.description: Review logs, notes, and drafts for incomplete setups, service problems, and recurring maintenance obligations.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Task List
prompt_templates.prompt: Sort me out using only [task list]. List pending work by urgency, owner, and next action. Do not change files or execute tasks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one approved source

prompt_templates.title: Find Forgotten Follow-Ups
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [approved notes] and [approved conversations] for forgotten promises and client follow-ups. Separate verified facts from assumptions. Do not contact anyone.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review commitments across several approved sources

prompt_templates.title: Verify Project Priorities
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [project] using [approved sources]. Verify status with read-only checks. Group urgent work, blockers, and forgotten items. Ask before writing or executing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review with current status checks

prompt_templates.title: Compare Recurring Reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [previous review] with [approved current sources]. Merge duplicates, rank financial impact, and identify changes. Propose actions and a dated note; await approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with history and approval boundaries

output_examples.input: Review my approved client notes and task list. Report only; do not take action.
output: Today, urgent: Send the revised proposal to Client A. Owner: you. Next action: approve the draft before the recorded deadline.
This week: Review the renewal reminder. Owner: you. Next action: confirm whether the service is still needed.
Waiting on someone else: Client B owes feedback. Waiting since Monday. Suggested nudge: Please confirm your preferred option.
Forgotten: The promised onboarding checklist remains unfinished. Owner: you. Next action: complete the missing section.
Done since last time: None verified. Payment status remains unverified because accounting access is unavailable.

output_examples.input: Compare the previous project review with current approved issue records. Do not modify the project.
output: Today, urgent: The release remains blocked by review. Owner: maintainer. Next action: request approval.
This week: Complete the migration checklist. Owner: developer. Duplicate reminders have been merged.
Waiting on someone else: Operations has not confirmed the maintenance window. Waiting since Tuesday. Suggested nudge: Please confirm the window.
Forgotten: The deployment guide still needs the rollback procedure. Owner: developer. Next action: draft the missing steps.
Done since last time: The current issue record confirms the test failure was resolved. No files were changed.

best_practices: Specify approved projects and sources before starting a review, especially when accounts contain unrelated client information.
Require read-only review and explicit approval before task execution, communications, or saving project notes.
Keep a dated review in an approved location, exclude secrets, and distinguish verified status from recorded claims.
anti_patterns: Treating access to an account as permission to review every project or execute every discovered task.
Presenting old notes as verified current status when no reliable check was available.
Saving credentials or unnecessary sensitive client details in the persistent review.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: One ordered review covering urgent work, weekly priorities, waiting items, forgotten commitments, and recently completed work.

faq.question: Does it connect to my inbox or calendar automatically?
faq.answer: It includes no bundled connectors. The host agent needs suitable tools and permission to access each source.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertain task status?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to distinguish checked facts from notes and clearly mark anything it could not verify.

faq.question: Will it perform tasks during the review?
faq.answer: The instructions direct immediate execution where possible, with exceptions for irreversible or paid actions. Explicitly require approval before any changes or communications.

faq.question: Can it track progress between reviews?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to save a timestamped list in project notes. Later reviews can compare that list with current accessible records.

faq.question: Can the review use my preferred language?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the agent to deliver the ordered answer in the user language.
